question.worked_solution:
q-78559:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,z=c$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,z & =c \\ {D}^{-1}D\,z & ={D}^{-1}c \\ {I}_{n}\,z & ={D}^{-1}\,c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and ${I}_{n}.$

q-78561:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,t=q$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,t & =q \\ {D}^{-1}D\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ {I}_{n}\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ t & ={D}^{-1}\,q\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and $q.$
